The National Association of Nigerian Students and the management of Osun State University on Tuesday differed over the arraignment of three officials of the institution’s Students’ Union Government in court for assault. Earlier, NANS National President, Babatunde Akinteye, in a statement obtained in Osogbo, the state capital, expressed concern over reports that the Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University, Prof. Clement Adebooye, allegedly ordered the arrest of the university’s SUG President. Akinteye also said the SUG President, after his arrest, was charged to court and remanded in prison, as he noted that the development was unacceptable and a direct affront to the rights and dignity of the students. The NANS President’s statement further read, “I have received disturbing reports that the Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University (UNIOSUN) allegedly ordered the arrest of the Students’ Union Government (SUG) President, who was subsequently charged to court and remanded in prison. “Consequently, I have directed the NANS Zonal Coordinator and the Osun State JCC Chairman to immediately mobilise students for a coordinated shutdown of the university and a peaceful occupation of the Osun State Government Secretariat to demand the immediate removal of the Vice-Chancellor. No university administrator should mistake the patience of Nigerian students for weakness. We will not fold our arms while the rights of our elected student representatives are trampled upon.” But the university management, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Ademola Adesoji, said it had temporarily suspended all students’ union activities following an “alleged assault involving three student union executives and a 100-level student of the institution.” Adesoji further disclosed that the decision was taken by the management to allow an investigation into the incident reported late Friday, November 20, 2026. He identified the student allegedly assaulted as Emmanuel Onifade, a 100-level Software Engineering student, while the three students accused of perpetrating the act were identified as Layonu Akintayo, a 500-level Medicine and Surgery student, who is the UNIOSUN SUG President; Adesanmi Tijesunimi, a 400-level Computer Science student and Assistant General Secretary of the union; and Oyedeji Samsideen, a 400-level Information Technology student and faculty chairman. Osun declares Friday public holiday for Adeleke’s inauguration Stop VCs from using NELFUND to hike fees, NANS tells Tinubu Adeleke backs grassroots sports as Osun marathon awards N2.55m The statement read, “Preliminary findings indicated that the incident followed allegations that Onifade had used the university’s logo and the Office of Student Affairs as the identity of a WhatsApp platform. “He was also accused of threatening Oyebode Oluwatobi Jomiloju Barnabas, a 200-level Computer Science student, over a video the latter had posted on social media concerning the university’s students. “Oyebode reported the matter to the students’ union executives, after which the union president contacted Onifade and asked him to meet at the Downtown area of the main campus. “Onifade was subsequently arrested by the students’ union in the union vehicle to a mechanic workshop in Osogbo, where he was thoroughly assaulted, beaten and brutalised by the Assistant General Secretary and others present. “It was further alleged that Onifade was taken to another location, where he met the students’ union president, and was assaulted again by the Assistant General Secretary and Samsideen. He was later released with serious bodily injuries. “The victim’s father subsequently reported the incident at the Oja-Oba Divisional Police Headquarters in Oke Baale, Osogbo. The three students were handed over to the police and later charged before a magistrate’s court in Oke-Fia, Osogbo. “They have reportedly been granted administrative bail, while the case has been adjourned until December 23, 2026.” Responding to the incident, Adesoji said the university has temporarily suspended all students’ union activities until the issues surrounding the event are resolved. He reaffirmed the university management’s commitment to the safety and welfare of students, and urged members of the UNIOSUN community to conduct themselves responsibly and in accordance with the law. The university said the suspension would remain in force until further notice. Bola Bamigbola
